title: Clubs on and around Central Avenue
summary: She and Willard sort out the Cotton Club, Bell Tavern, Apex, Club Alabam and Curtis Mosby's role.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: In Culver City, that's right. And then out south you had the Bell Tavern.
Right. I think it was in Gardena, because
you had all those little towns, but I think it was in Gardena. But, you know, you had those things.
Then on Central Avenue, my gracious me, every little place, every little bar on Central Avenue or anywhere, had entertainment, some type of entertainment. It was just marvelous.
What were the names of them? Which clubs were operating when you first came out here?

Well, as I say, I mentioned the Club Alabam, and I mentioned -- I think there was a club at that time called the Apex also that was down the street, and of course Curtis Mosby had a place, I think he had a place that later became the Apex, I think. And later on Curtis Mosby became the manager or something, or the owner of the Club Alabam.
Yeah. I know he did run an Apex and --
-- an Alabam, but at one point someone said the Alabam was run by a couple of Italian brothers.
Yeah, well it was, but I think this was after -- I think it was before, I mean, before Mosby's time.
I think Curtis came into the picture later, see. So --
And the Alabam was the largest club on Central Avenue, wasn't it?
It was the most popular, I can tell you that. It was the most popular.

It was later on that I went to all the clubs, but at the time I went to them the Alabam was still open and the Alabam was the largest and the most lavish and it had floor shows along with whatever music.
